description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) of different methods as a function of the co-occurrence number. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^3. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)," ranges from 60% to 80%. The plot includes six lines, each representing a different method: Base (black line with circle markers), MEND (brown line with diamond markers), FT (blue line with triangle markers), MEMIT (purple line with pentagon markers), IKE (red line with triangle markers), and ROME (green line with square markers). The Base line starts at approximately 62% accuracy at the lowest co-occurrence number and ends at around 67% at the highest co-occurrence number. The MEND line begins at about 65% and ends near 72%. The FT line starts at roughly 63% and finishes close to 68%. The MEMIT line begins at approximately 64% and ends at about 71%. The IKE line starts at around 64% and ends near 69%. The ROME line begins at about 66% and ends at approximately 73%. All lines show a general upward trend, indicating an increase in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases.
